issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of convergence for η∈(0,1) when δ_t→2, the residual of the full trajectory satisfies L_{t+1}=g_η(L_t)+ε_t, ε_t→0, and Proposition prop:asymptotic_tracking_vanishing_perturbations (and its finite-horizon tracking estimate Eq. (eq:finite_horizon_tracking_rho)) is invoked with K=[-1,1]. That proposition has the standing hypothesis (x_t)⊂K, used essentially in its proof: Step 1 concludes x_{t+1}∈U only because x_{t+1}∈K excludes membership in K\U via |ε_t|<γ₀, and Step 2 bounds |f(x)-f(y)| by the modulus of continuity on K. The containment (L_t)⊂[-1,1] is never verified and is false in general: on a certified trajectory |L_t|≤2/δ_t with δ_t<2, so |L_t|>1 is admissible (e.g. η=0.5, (a₀,b₀)=(2,-0.5) is certified with L₀=2), and no argument confines L_t to [-1,1] at the tracking times t_k,…,t_k+N or for all t≥t_*. The applications of the tracking estimate and of the proposition are therefore invalid as written.

issues.failure_explanation: Axioms A1–A7 constrain only the nested collection of level sets and their interaction with the GD map, and every one of them is invariant under replacing P(δ) by P_spec(φ(δ)) for any increasing bijection φ:(0,2]→(0,2] (the threshold in A5/A6 becomes φ⁻¹(η)); such a reparametrized family satisfies all the axioms yet P̃(δ)≠P_spec(δ), so 'P(δ) is uniquely determined' and the displayed formula as a function of δ are false as stated. The Lagrange analysis establishes only that a level set containing an unbalanced minimizer x_* must be the specific ellipse with parameter 4a_*²/(a_*⁴+1) — a parameter tied to the minimizer, not to the level set's δ-label — so the concluding inference that each level set is forced to coincide with the same-δ level set of the specific family is a non sequitur. Only uniqueness of the nested family of level sets up to monotone reparametrization of the state variable is supported.

issues.failure_explanation: Admissibility of a pair (δ,ξ) is defined by the one-step monotonicity test at a given step size η. The concluding sentence claims numerical evidence for an admissible branch on the full interval δ∈(0,2) for every σ∈(0,1] without qualifying the step size; but the paper's own observation (ii) reports that at the tested step size η=0.6 the pass region is empty below a σ-dependent δ-threshold, i.e., no admissible branch on the full interval exists at that step size. Full-interval admissibility is observed only at η=0.2, and σ=1 is untested, so the summary asserts a materially broader scope than the reported experiments establish.
